title: Triage: the facts decide the route
description: A risky task goes to the reviewed route when it is small, otherwise to the pipeline. A task that is not risky goes to the pipeline when it touches 12 or more files or splits into parallel slices, and to a plain session otherwise. The fifth fact, code, sets the file count for parallel slices (10 for code, 4 otherwise); it also decides whether git worktrees are used and, in headless runs, whether web tools are allowed.
notes: Small: at most 3 files, at most 200 lines and one slice. Parallel: 2 or more independent slices and either 1,500 or more lines or enough files: 10 for code (minParallelFilesCode, raised from 4 after a 2-rep, coding-only benchmark, docs/benchmarks.md), 4 for work that changes no code (minParallelFilesNonCode, the earlier default; nothing measured non-code work). See src/config.ts TRIAGE.

The fifth fact, code (the task changes source, tests, build or CI configuration in a repository), changes only that file threshold in src/triage.ts decide(); a missing code counts as code (src/triage.ts:12-20, 88-93). Callers also use it to decide whether git machinery (worktrees, checkpoint commits, the integrator) is used and, in npm run auto, whether web tools are allowed (scripts/auto.sh); the test gate decides from the changed files, not from code (.claude/hooks/verify.sh).
